title: Hedging and Diplomacy in Academic Discussion / Kɔbɔ sɛnea waka asɛm ne nnwuma ho asɛm a ɛyɛ den wɔ akadeemik asɛm bɛba mu
bridge: Wɔ Akadeemik Ingelisi kasa mu, kɔbɔ sɛnea waka asɛm (hedging) yɛ den sɛnea ɛbɛka sɛ woyɛ pɛnkyeɛ nea ɛyɛ adwuma a ɛyɛ den. Sɛnea ɛbɛka sɛ woyɛ pɛnkyeɛ nea ɛyɛ adwuma a ɛyɛ den. rule: Kɔbɔ sɛnea waka asɛm wɔ Akadeemik Ingelisi kasa mu: 1) Kɔbɔ sɛnea waka asɛm a ɛyɛ den: might, may, could (e.g. 'This might indicate...'). 2) Kɔbɔ sɛnea waka asɛm a ɛyɛ den: I would argue, I tend to think, I feel. 3) Kɔbɔ sɛnea waka asɛm a ɛyɛ den: perhaps, possibly, arguably, seemingly, apparently. 4) Kɔbɔ sɛnea waka asɛm a ɛyɛ den: suggests, indicates, implies, appears (instead of 'proves' or 'shows'). 5) Kɔbɔ sɛnea waka asɛm a ɛyɛ den: it could be argued that, it seems that, one might consider. 6) Kɔbɔ sɛnea waka asɛm a ɛyɛ den: not entirely, not necessarily, not wholly (e.g. 'not entirely convincing'). 7) Kɔbɔ sɛnea waka asɛm a ɛyɛ den: somewhat, rather, fairly (e.g. 'somewhat controversial'). 8) Kɔbɔ sɛnea waka asɛm a ɛyɛ den: if this were the case, it would... Nnipa a wɔyɛ den: mmom 'must' ne 'definitely' wɔ akadeemik asɛm mu (ɛsɛe sɛ wɔyɛ pɛnkyeɛ); mmom 'very' (use 'highly', 'considerably'); ne sɛ wɔ Twi 'creo que' ɛyɛ den sɛ 'I think' wɔ Ingelisi, nanso wɔ akadeemik asɛm mu 'I would argue' anaa 'It seems to me' yɛ den. Mmusuo: wɔ akadeemik asɛm mu ɛbɛyɛ pɛnkyeɛ (e.g. 'This demonstrates...'), nanso ɛsɛe sɛ 'strongly suggests'.

translations.tw: Asɛm bɛba mu wɔ akadeemik seminar mu

title: Strategic Hedging & Diplomatic Language / Asɛm a ɛsɛe ne Asɛm a ɛyɛ Adwuma
bridge: Wɔ Twi mu, ɛyɛ adwuma a wɔrebɛ fa so a wɔbɛkae kan a wɔbɛkae, sɛ 'nea ɛbɛyɛ', 'nea ɛbɛyɛ' anaa subjunctive, noko wɔ English a wɔde bɛyɛ adwuma mu, wɔde modal adverbs (sɛ, perhaps, arguably) ne 'hedging verbs' sɛ 'seem', 'appear', 'tend to' de. Sɛnea Adwuma a wɔde bɛyɛ no, ɛyɛ sɛ wɔde 'I think' de maa 'I believe' wɔ British English a ɛyɛ formal, na ɛno ara nso ɛyɛ sɛ wɔde 'creo' de maa ɛyɛ neutral.
rule: Wɔ English a wɔde bɛyɛ adwuma mu, 'hedging' (atenuation) ɛba mu sɛ: 1) Modal adverbs: perhaps, possibly, arguably, presumably, allegedly (position a ɛwɔ awie anaa awie). 2) Perception verbs: seem, appear, tend to, suggest (wɔde bɛkae kan a wɔbɛkae). 3) Modals: might, may, could (ɛso wɔhɔ sɛ 'must' anaa 'will'). 4) Expressions sɛ 'It could be argued that...', 'One might say that...' (wɔde bɛkae kan a wɔbɛkae). 5) Adjectives: 'a bit', 'slightly', 'somewhat' (wɔde bɛto so). Sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ, wɔ Twi mu, wɔde subjunctive maa duda, noko wɔ English mu, wɔde modal + base form (without -s). Example: 'Es posible que esté equivocado' → 'It is possible that I am wrong' (not 'I be wrong'). Wɔ meetings mu, wɔde 'I'd suggest we consider...' de maa 'We should change...'. Sɛ wopɛ sɛ wobɛkae kan a wɔbɛkae, de 'I see your point, but have we considered...?' (ɛmma 'No, that's wrong'). C1 level no, ɛsɛ sɛ: 'I'm not entirely convinced that...' vs. 'I have reservations about...'.

translations.tw: Adwuma a ɛyɛ mmerɛw a wɔde bɛyɛ

title: Nuanced Literary Analysis: Register, Tone, and Implied Meaning / Nnyinasosae Adwuma Wosɔreɛ: Nkyea, Ahomaso, ne Nnyinasosae
bridge: Wɔ Twi, yɛbɛka subjunctive structures ne explicit rhetorical devices sɛ yɛbɛfa so ama yɛbɛka nnyinasoɛ ne nnyinasoɛ a wɔ wosɔreɛ no ho asɛm. Wɔ English, C1 kyerɛ sɛ wo werɛ hyia sɛ woka modal verbs (might, could, would), passive voice a wɔfa so ama wɔbɛyɛ distance, ne vocabulary a wɔde kyerɛkyerɛ asɛm pɛpɛɛpɛ. Hispanohablantes no betumi ayɛ sɛ wɔbɛde 'es posible que...' bɛyɛ 'it is possible that...' wɔ literal, nanso English pɛ sɛ wɔbɛde adverbials (arguably, ostensibly) anaa modal verbs ama wɔbɛma nnyinasoɛ, na ɛsɛ sɛ wɔyɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ wɔ present historic ne past perfect a wɔde kyerɛkyerɛ ne ama wɔbɛka literary works ho asɛm.
rule:
Saa wopɛ sɛ woyɛ literary ne cultural analysis a ɛwɔ C1 level wɔ English a, ɛsɛ sɛ wɔmfa nhyehyɛɛ:
1. **Formal ne academic register**: Fa verbs sɛ *suggest, imply, illustrate, portray* na ɛnkyɛ *show* anaa *tell*, ne discourse markers (however, moreover, consequently).
2. **Modality a wɔde kyerɛkyerɛ certainty degrees**: *Must* sɛ wopɛ sɛ woyɛ logical deductions, *might/may* sɛ wopɛ sɛ woyɛ possibilities, ne *could* sɛ wopɛ sɛ woyɛ suggestions. Contrast with Twi, befiri sɛ nnyinasoɛ a wɔde kyerɛkyerɛ no asɛm no asɛm no wɔ subjunctive: 'Quizás el autor intentara...' bɛyɛ 'The author might be trying...' anaa 'Perhaps the author is trying...'.
3. **Passive voice ne 'it' passive**: Ama wɔayɛ distance ne ama wɔde ma asɛm no yɛ objective (it is argued, it could be said). Wɔ Twi, 'se' impersonal no yɛ common, nanso wɔ English no wɔfa passive.
4. **Present historic**: Ama wɔbɛka plot events (In Chapter 3, the protagonist meets...), na wɔ Twi no wɔde present anaa past tense ama wɔbɛka detailed narratives.
5. **Structures a wɔde kyerɛkyerɛ purpose ne cause**: *in order to, so as to, with the aim of* vs. 'para', ne *due to, owing to* vs. 'debido a'.

translations.tw: Nnyinasosae Adwuma Wosɔreɛ ne Abakɔsɛm a Ɛyɛ Den

title: The Art of Nuance: Hedging and Speculating / Nnwonwa ne Nnweduro: Adwuma ne Nnwuma
bridge: Wɔ Twi, mmusuanyi a wɔde kasa no wɔ’gyaw ne kondisional sɛ wɔbɛma ara sɛ wɔnnyɛ adanse (e.g., 'Ebia ɔbɛba'). Wɔ English, nnweduro no ma wɔde modal verbs, adverbs ne mfatoho a wɔwɔ hɔ bio sɛ 'may well', 'might as well' anaa 'I dare say'. Nnipa a wɔkasa Twi no adi kan sɛ wɔnnyɛ adanse wɔ English no mu, efisɛ English no nni nnweduro a ɛso wɔ hɔ bio, na ɛnyɛ den sɛ wɔde 'maybe' di ka bio. Ɛsɛ sɛ woahu nnweduro a ɛwɔ hɔ bio wɔ nnwuma ne nnweduro no so sɛ wɔbɛma wo kasa sɛ ɛte sɛ ɛyɛ den ne ɛte sɛ ɛyɛ pɛ.
rule: Sɛ wopɛ sɛ wɔde nnweduro ne adwuma wɔ English C1 no, woade: 1) Modal verbs a wɔwɔ hɔ bio (may, might, could, should, ought to) ne nnweduro a wɔwɔ hɔ bio. 2) Mfatoho a wɔwɔ hɔ bio wɔ akɔntaa no mu (might have, could have) sɛ wɔbɛka nnweduro wɔ akɔntaa no mu. 3) Adverbs ne mfatoho a wɔwɔ hɔ bio sɛ wɔbɛma ara sɛ wɔnnyɛ adanse: arguably, presumably, allegedly, in all likelihood, by any stretch of the imagination. 4) Mfatoho a wɔde ma ara sɛ wɔnnyɛ adanse sɛ 'I would venture to say', 'It stands to reason that', 'One might argue that'. 5) Nnweduro a ɛde 'should/were' sɛ wɔbɛka nnweduro a ɛte sɛ ɛyɛ den. 6) 'Seem/appear' de ma infinitive anaa that-clause sɛ wɔbɛma ara sɛ wɔnnyɛ adanse. Nnweduro a ɛte sɛ ɛyɛ den: wɔnnyɛ nnweduro a ɛso wɔ hɔ bio; adverbs no wɔ hɔ a wɔde ma ara sɛ wɔnnyɛ adanse, nanso ɛnyɛ den sɛ wɔde ma ara sɛ wɔnnyɛ adanse bio; 'maybe' yɛ informal na wɔnnyɛ wɔn wɔ mfatoho a ɛte sɛ ɛyɛ den, na wɔde 'perhaps' anaa 'possibly' di ka.

translations.tw: Ntamɔ ne Ntamɔ a Ɛyɛ Den

title: Nuanced Political Commentary / Nkitahodi a wɔde ama nnipa asɛm
bridge: Wɔ Twi, yɛnka ɛno a wɔde ama nnipa asɛm ma ɛno a wɔde ama nnipa asɛm. Wɔ Gyeman ne Frɛnkye, wɔde kyerɛw kronkron ne mmerɛa (might, could, should) ne mfatoho a wɔatwa nkyerɛaseɛ no ho asɛm (it is argued that) ma ɛno a wɔde ama nnipa asɛm. Faako a wɔbɛka 'es probable que' ma 'it is probable that' a ɛte sɛn, na Gyeman ne Frɛnkyefoɔ pɛ 'it is likely to' anaa 'it may well be that'. Afeɛ, wɔ Gyeman ne Frɛnkye, wɔde kyerɛw kronkron ne mmerɛa (utterly, profoundly, slightly) ma ɛno a wɔde ama nnipa asɛm, na wɔ Twi, yɛnka ɛno a wɔde ama nnipa asɛm ma ɛno a wɔde ama nnipa asɛm.
rule: Ma nnipa asɛm a wɔde ama nnipa asɛm wɔ Gyeman ne Frɛnkye (C1), wɔde: 1) Kyerɛw kronkron a wɔde kyerɛw nnipa asɛm: 'might', 'could', 'may', 'should' (e.g., 'The policy might backfire'). 2) Mfatoho a wɔatwa nkyerɛaseɛ no ho asɛm: 'it is argued', 'it has been suggested', 'it is widely believed'. 3) Kyerɛw kronkron ne mmerɛa: 'profound', 'utterly', 'deeply', 'marginally'. 4) Mmerɛa a wɔde kyerɛw nnipa asɛm: 'while', 'whereas', 'even though'. 5) Mfatoho a wɔde kyerɛw nnipa asɛm: 'tend to'. Faako a wɔbɛka 'I think'; de 'I would argue', 'It seems to me'. Faako sɛ wɔ Gyeman ne Frɛnkye, wɔnka ɛno a wɔde ama nnipa asɛm (except wɔ mmerɛa a wɔatwa nkyerɛaseɛ no ho asɛm sɛ 'suffice it to say') na wɔde 'should' anaa ɛno a wɔde ama nnipa asɛm.

concept_examples.text: The government's approach to immigration could be described as profoundly misguided.
concept_examples.translation: Sɛnea government no rekɔ ha a wɔde ama nnipa asɛm, ɛba sɛ ɛyɛ den a ɛyɛ den.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ðə ˈɡʌvənmənts əˈproʊtʃ tə ˌɪmɪˈɡreɪʃən kʊd bi dɪˈskraɪbd æz prəˈfaʊndli ˌmɪsˈɡaɪdɪd/

concept_examples.text: It is widely argued that economic sanctions rarely achieve their intended objectives.

concept_examples.phonetic: /ɪt ɪz ˈwaɪdli ˈɑːrɡjuːd ðæt ˌiːkəˈnɑːmɪk ˈsæŋkʃənz ˈrerli əˈtʃiːv ðeər ɪnˈtendɪd əbˈdʒektɪvz/

concept_examples.text: While the reform has brought some benefits, it has also exacerbated social inequality.

concept_examples.text: The rhetoric of populism tends to oversimplify complex economic realities.
concept_examples.translation: Sɛnea wɔde ama nnipa asɛm, ɛba sɛ ɛyɛ den a ɛyɛ den.

common_error.correct: The new law is likely to cause more problems.
common_error.correct_alt: The new law could well cause more problems.

Gyeman ne Frɛnkyefoɔ pɛ 'be likely to' anaa 'could well' ma ɛno a wɔde ama nnipa asɛm. 'It is probable that' ɛte sɛn wɔ mmerɛa a wɔatwa nkyerɛaseɛ no ho asɛm, na wɔ nnipa asɛm a wɔde ama nnipa asɛm, wɔde mfatoho a ɛte sɛn.

examples.original: The negotiations could easily break down over the issue of border control.

examples.original: However appealing the proposal sounds, it is economically unviable.

examples.original: The opposition's rhetoric borders on xenophobia, albeit more subtly than before.
examples.phonetic: /ði ˌɑːpəˈzɪʃənz ˈretərɪk ˈbɔːrdərz ɒn ˌzenəˈfoʊbiə, ɔːlˈbiːɪt mɔːr ˈsʌtli ðæn bɪˈfɔːr/
examples.translation: Sɛnea wɔde ama nnipa asɛm, ɛba sɛ ɛyɛ den a ɛyɛ den.
examples.note: 'Borders on' kyerɛw sɛ ɛyɛ den a ɛyɛ den; 'albeit' kyerɛw sɛ ɛyɛ den a ɛyɛ den (ɛte sɛ 'aunque').

examples.original: The minister's statement is a blatant attempt to scapegoat immigrants for economic woes.
examples.phonetic: /ðə ˈmɪnɪstərz ˈsteɪtmənt ɪz ə ˈbleɪtənt əˈtempt tə ˈskeɪpɡoʊt ˈɪmɪɡrənts fɔːr ˌiːkəˈnɑːmɪk woʊz/

examples.phonetic: /ðɪs ɪz ə ˈklæsɪk keɪs əv pəˈlɪtɪkəl ˈɡrændstændɪŋ, wɪtʃ ˌʌndərˈmaɪnz ˈdʒenjuɪn dɪˈbeɪt/
examples.translation: Sɛnea wɔde ama nnipa asɛm, ɛba sɛ ɛyɛ den a ɛyɛ den.
examples.note: 'Grandstanding' kyerɛw sɛ ɛyɛ den a ɛyɛ den. De 'which' ma ɛno a wɔde ama nnipa asɛm.

translations.tw: Nkitahodi a wɔde ama nnipa asɛm

title: Narratives with Perspective / Nkyerɛaseɛ ne Nnawota
bridge: Wɔ Twi, sɛ yɛbɛka ho asɛm a ɛdɔɔso no, yɛnkyea ahyɛaseɛ a ɛfiri nnawota foforo na yɛde kyerɛ asɛm no ho nhyehyɛeɛ ne ahyɛaseɛ a ɛfiri nnawota a ɛyɛ den na ɛyɛ mmerɛw no ho nhyehyɛeɛ. Wɔ English, ahyɛaseɛ a ɛfiri nnawota a ɛyɛ den ('past simple') ne ahyɛaseɛ a ɛfiri nnawota a ɛyɛ mmerɛw ('past continuous') no ho nto nyinaa te sɛn ka, nanso ahyɛaseɛ a ɛfiri nnawota a ɛyɛ den pii ('past perfect') no ho nhyehyɛeɛ ne ahyɛaseɛ a ɛfiri nnawota a ɛyɛ mmerɛw pii ('past perfect continuous') no ho nhyehyɛeɛ wɔ English no yɛ mmerɛw pii wɔ Twi. Adɛn nti, Twi mmebɔpa no biara wɔ hɔ a ɛbɛka ahyɛaseɛ a ɛfiri nnawota a ɛyɛ den ('past simple') no ho nhyehyɛeɛ wɔ English no, na ɛbɛka ahyɛaseɛ a ɛfiri nnawota a ɛyɛ mmerɛw ('past continuous') no ho nhyehyɛeɛ, na ɛbɛka ahyɛaseɛ a ɛfiri nnawota a ɛyɛ den pii ('past perfect') no ho nhyehyɛeɛ.
rule: Sɛ wubɛka nkyerɛaseɛ a ɛyɛ den wɔ English no (CEFR C1), fa ahyɛaseɛ a ɛfiri nnawota no mmienu ansa na wode kyerɛ asɛm no ho nhyehyɛeɛ ne mmusuedan no. Ahyɛaseɛ a ɛfiri nnawota a ɛyɛ den ('past simple') no de kyerɛ asɛm a ɛyɛ den na ɛyɛ mmerɛw. Ahyɛaseɛ a ɛfiri nnawota a ɛyɛ mmerɛw ('past continuous') no de kyerɛ asɛm a ɛyɛ mmerɛw wɔ nnawota a ɛdɔɔso no. Ahyɛaseɛ a ɛfiri nnawota a ɛyɛ den pii ('past perfect') no de kyerɛ asɛm a ɛyɛ den pii wɔ nnawota a ɛdɔɔso no. Ahyɛaseɛ a ɛfiri nnawota a ɛyɛ mmerɛw pii ('past perfect continuous') no de kyerɛ asɛm a ɛyɛ mmerɛw pii wɔ nnawota a ɛdɔɔso no. Sɛ wubɛka ho asɛm a ɛyɛ den (ntwɛm, adwene, nea woyɛ, anaa nkyerɛaseɛ a ɛfiri nnawota foforo), fa 'would' de ma ahyɛaseɛ a ɛfiri nnawota a ɛyɛ den no, 'used to' de ma ahyɛaseɛ a ɛfiri nnawota a ɛyɛ mmerɛw no, na mmusuedan a ɛfiri nnawota foforo a wɔde kyerɛ asɛm a ɛyɛ den pii ('might have' anaa 'could have') de ma ahyɛaseɛ a ɛfiri nnawota a ɛyɛ den pii no.

concept_examples.text: I had already left the office when she called, so I missed her message.
concept_examples.translation: Ɛda a mefa no, ɛno ara na ɔree frɛɛ me, na ɛno nti na mehu ɔhaw no.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪ hæd ɔːlˈrɛdi lɛft ði ˈɒfɪs wɛn ʃiː kɔːld, səʊ aɪ mɪst hɜː ˈmɛsɪdʒ/

concept_examples.text: She was reading the report for hours, and she still didn't notice the mistake.
concept_examples.translation: Ɔkɔ so ara na ɔkenkane hyɛne nhoma no mu, na ɛno nti na ɔnhu ɔhaw no.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʃiː wɒz ˈriːdɪŋ ðə rɪˈpɔːt fə ˈaʊəz, ənd ʃiː stɪl ˈdɪdnt ˈnəʊtɪs ðə mɪsˈteɪk/

concept_examples.text: By the time we arrived, the train had already left; we had been stuck in traffic for two hours.
concept_examples.translation: Sɛ yɛbɛa no, trotro no na ɛyɛɛ, na yɛn ara na yɛkɔɔ ntɛntɛmu no mu, na yɛkɔɔ mu no, yɛkɔɔ mu no ho nhyehyɛeɛ no, yɛkɔɔ mu no ho nhyehyɛeɛ no bi.
concept_examples.phonetic: /baɪ ðə taɪm wiː əˈraɪvd, ðə treɪn hæd ɔːlˈrɛdi lɛft; wiː hæd biːn stʌk ɪn ˈtræfɪk fə tuː ˈaʊəz/

concept_examples.text: He used to live in Madrid, but he would often travel to Barcelona for work.
concept_examples.translation: Me ne me koma no yɛɛ Madrid, nanso ɛno ara na yɛkɔɔ Barcelona ma wɔn a wɔyɛ adwuma no.
concept_examples.phonetic: /hiː juːst tə lɪv ɪn məˈdrɪd, bʌt hiː wʊd ˈɒfən ˈtrævl tə ˌbɑːsəˈloʊnə fə wɜːk/

common_error.wrong: I was already leaving the office when she called, so I missed her message.
common_error.correct: I had already left the office when she called, so I missed her message.
common_error.correct_alt: I had already been leaving the office when she called (less natural).
common_error.explanation: Ɛhaw no baa nti, wɔ Twi, wɔde ahyɛaseɛ a ɛfiri nnawota a ɛyɛ mmerɛw ('salía') ma asɛm a ɛyɛ mmerɛw a ɛyɛ den no. Wɔ English, sɛ asɛm no yɛ den pii no, wɔde ahyɛaseɛ a ɛfiri nnawota a ɛyɛ den pii ('had left') ma no. Ahyɛaseɛ a ɛfiri nnawota a ɛyɛ mmerɛw ('was leaving') no kyerɛ sɛ ɔka ho asɛm wɔ nnawota no, na ɛmmɛka sɛ ɔyɛɛ no. Sɛ wubɛka ɛhaw no, su asɛm no sɛ ɛyɛ den anaa ɛyɛ mmerɛw wɔ nnawota a ɛdɔɔso no. Sɛ asɛm no yɛ den pii no, fa ahyɛaseɛ a ɛfiri nnawota a ɛyɛ den pii ('past perfect') de ma no.

levels.label: Narrative Tenses: Sequence and Background
levels.translation: Ahyɛaseɛ a ɛfiri nnawota: ntɛm ne ahyɛaseɛ a ɛfiri nnawota

examples.original: When I entered the room, she was writing a letter and the radio was playing softly.
examples.phonetic: /wɛn aɪ ˈɛntəd ðə ruːm, ʃiː wɒz ˈraɪtɪŋ ə ˈlɛtər ənd ðə ˈreɪdiəʊ wɒz ˈpleɪɪŋ ˈsɒftli/
examples.translation: Sɛ mebɛa baako a, ɔno ara na ɔkɔ so ara na ɔde kyerɛw no mu, na ɛno ara na ɛdeɛ no.
examples.note: Fa 'past simple' de ma asɛm a ɛyɛ den no (entered) na 'past continuous' de ma ahyɛaseɛ a ɛfiri nnawota no (was writing, was playing).

examples.original: We were walking home when it started to rain, so we took shelter under a tree.
examples.phonetic: /wiː wɜː ˈwɔːkɪŋ həʊm wɛn ɪt ˈstɑːtɪd tə reɪn, səʊ wiː tʊk ˈʃɛltər ˈʌndər ə triː/
examples.translation: Yɛkɔɔ mu no, yɛkɔɔ mu no ho nhyehyɛeɛ no, yɛkɔɔ mu no ho nhyehyɛeɛ no bi.
examples.note: Wɔ Twi, 'caminábamos' (ahyɛaseɛ a ɛfiri nnawota a ɛyɛ mmerɛw) no de kyerɛ 'past continuous' wɔ English no ho nhyehyɛeɛ no, na 'empezó' (ahyɛaseɛ a ɛfiri nnawota a ɛyɛ den) no de kyerɛ 'past simple'.

examples.original: She had finished the report before the meeting started.
examples.phonetic: /ʃiː hæd ˈfɪnɪʃt ðə rɪˈpɔːt bɪˈfɔː ðə ˈmiːtɪŋ ˈstɑːtɪd/
examples.translation: Ɔno ara na ɔde kyerɛw no mu no, ɛno ara na ɛdeɛ no.
examples.note: Ahyɛaseɛ a ɛfiri nnawota a ɛyɛ den pii ('past perfect') no de kyerɛ asɛm a ɛyɛ den pii. Wɔ Twi, wɔde 'había terminado' anaa 'terminó' ma no sɛ ɛyɛ den pii, nanso wɔ English, wɔde 'had finished' ma no.

levels.label: Past Perfect and Past Perfect Continuous
levels.translation: Ahyɛaseɛ a ɛfiri nnawota a ɛyɛ den pii ne ahyɛaseɛ a ɛfiri nnawota a ɛyɛ mmerɛw pii

examples.original: He had been working at that company for ten years before he decided to quit.

examples.translation: Ɔno ara na ɔkɔ so ara na ɔde kyerɛw no mu no, ɛno ara na ɛdeɛ no.
examples.note: Ahyɛaseɛ a ɛfiri nnawota a ɛyɛ mmerɛw pii ('past perfect continuous') no de kyerɛ asɛm a ɛyɛ mmerɛw pii. Wɔ Twi, 'había estado trabajando' no yɛ kwan, nanso wɔde 'llevaba diez años trabajando' ma no.

examples.original: They had just arrived when the news broke.
examples.phonetic: /ðeɪ hæd dʒʌst əˈraɪvd wɛn ðə njuːz brəʊk/
examples.translation: Wɔbɛa no, wɔbɛa no ho nhyehyɛeɛ no, wɔbɛa no ho nhyehyɛeɛ no bi.
examples.note: Adwuma a ɛfiri nnawota a ɛyɛ den ('just') ne ahyɛaseɛ a ɛfiri nnawota a ɛyɛ den pii ('past perfect') no de kyerɛ asɛm a ɛyɛ den. Wɔ Twi, wɔde 'acabar de' ma no wɔ ahyɛaseɛ a ɛfiri nnawota a ɛyɛ mmerɛw ('acababan de llegar'), nanso wɔ English, wɔde 'had just arrived' ma no.

examples.original: She was exhausted because she had been studying all night.
examples.phonetic: /ʃiː wɒz ɪɡˈzɔːstɪd bɪˈkɒz ʃiː hæd biːn ˈstʌdiɪŋ ɔːl naɪt/

levels.label: Habits and Speculation in the Past
levels.translation: Nnawota ne adwene wɔ nnawota a ɛdɔɔso

examples.note: 'Used to' de ma ahyɛaseɛ anaa ahyɛaseɛ a ɛfiri nnawota a ɛyɛ mmerɛw a ɛyɛ den no. Ɛyɛ mmerɛw sɛ wubɛka ahyɛaseɛ a ɛfiri nnawota a ɛyɛ den ne ahyɛaseɛ a ɛfiri nnawota a ɛyɛ mmerɛw no. Hwehwe 'would' wɔ hɔ, efisɛ ɛyɛ ahyɛaseɛ a ɛfiri nnawota a ɛyɛ mmerɛw, na ɛmmɛyɛ ahyɛaseɛ a ɛfiri nnawota a ɛyɛ den.

translations.tw: Nkyerɛaseɛ a ɛyɛ den ne nnawota

title: Advanced debate techniques / Nnyinasoɔm ne ahoɔden a wɔatwa mu
bridge: Wɔ Twi, ahoɔden a wɔatwa mu biara, wɔkyerɛw wɔde mmoaano bɛka awoɔ a ɛte saa 'nanso' anaa 'nkyerɛaseɛ' no, nanso wɔ English no, mmoaano ne ahoɔden a wɔatwa no ma wɔde ahoɔden a ɛso awaree pii: 'although it may be true that...', 'even if we agree that...', 'be that as it may...'. Anaa, wɔde asɛm a ɛso awaree ne a ɛte sɛn kyɛn biara kyerɛɛ wɔatwa pii sɛn kyɛn biara sɛ 'I understand your point, but...' ɛso awaree pii sɛn kyɛn biara. Hwɛ kyerɛ sɛ 'of course' ɛnyɛ 'nkyerɛaseɛ' wɔ ahoɔden a wɔatwa mu: wɔ nnyinasoɔm mu, 'admittedly' anaa 'granted' ɛso awaree pii. Afe ha, wɔde 'on the contrary' kyerɛɛ 'nanso' wɔ kyerɛw a ɛso awaree pii, nanso wɔ English no, wɔde yɛn kyerɛw a ɛso awaree pii.
rule: Ma wɔde ahoɔden a wɔatwa mu wɔ English no, hwɛ ɛha: 1) Mmoaano + ahoɔden: 'Although it is true that [X], it is also true that [Y]' anaa 'Even if we agree that [X], we must still consider [Y]'. Wɔ Twi no, yɛde 'nanso' anaa 'nkyerɛaseɛ' kyerɛɛ mmoaano, nanso wɔ English no, yɛnntɔn 'while' a ɛso awaree pii. 2) Ahoɔden a ɛso awaree pii: 'That argument is not valid because...', 'This is a false equivalence fallacy', 'I disagree with the premise that...'. 3) Mmoaano a ɛso awaree pii: 'I understand your point, but...', 'Respectfully, I disagree', 'That may be true, but...'. Mma 'yes, but' a ɛso awaree pii; de 'however', 'nevertheless', 'nonetheless', nanso hwɛ kyerɛ sɛ ɛha koma, na ɛnyɛ 'although' (a ɛnnhwɛ koma). 4) Ahoɔden a ɛso awaree pii: 'Consider the counterexample of...', 'This is contradicted by the fact that...'. 5) De modals ma wɔde ahoɔden a ɛso awaree pii: 'That might be true, but...', 'You could argue that, yet...'. Wɔ Twi no, yɛde 'nanso' pii; wɔ English no, ma wɔde 'however' anaa 'though' ma wɔde ahoɔden a ɛso awaree pii.

translations.tw: Nnyinasoɔm ne ahoɔden a wɔatwa mu

title: Navigating Academic Discourse / Asɛm a ɛtɔ Nwoma ne Nnɔmba
bridge: Wɔ Twi mu, asɛm a ɛtɔ nwoma ne nnɔmba biara so sɛe wɔ nominalizations ne structures a ɛnnyɛ personal, nanso wɔ English mu, ɛkyerɛw ne a wɔde subject no hyɛ paa, na wɔde passive voice hyɛm biara. Ɛyɛ den a ɔkɔ so sɛ wɔbɛka subjunctive ne asɛm a ɛte saa 'it is important that' wɔ English mu, na wɔpɛ 'it is important to' anaa 'it is crucial that' ne subjunctive wɔ some registers mu. Bio, English a ɛtɔ nwoma ne nnɔmba biara so sɛe wɔ verbs a wɔde 'report' (e.g., 'suggest', 'argue') wɔ mfatoho a ɛyɛ den pɛ, na Twi nea ɛyɛ ɛno a ɛyɛ circumlocutory. Fa akwantu ne adverbials asɛm no ho nhyehyɛ.
rule: Saa wɔbɛka asɛm a ɛtɔ nwoma ne nnɔmba biara so wɔ English mu wɔ C1 level no, ɛsɛ sɛ woadi: (1) Verbs a wɔde research ne argumentation (e.g., 'suggest', 'argue', 'maintain', 'contend') a wɔde 'that' + clause ne verb wɔ base form (subjunctive) wɔ formal contexts (e.g., 'The study suggests that the effect be considered'). (2) Lexical collocations a ɛtɔ register no (e.g., 'draw a conclusion', 'pose a question', 'address an issue', 'make a case'). (3) Formal discourse connectors (e.g., 'furthermore', 'however', 'conversely', 'in light of') a wɔde kyerɛ ideas a wɔrekɔ so. (4) Passive voice wɔ perfect ne modal tenses (e.g., 'has been argued', 'might be attributed to') sɛdeɛ ɛbɛma ɛyɛ objective. (5) Nominalizations a wɔaka '-tion', '-ment', '-ness' (e.g., 'implementation', 'assessment') sɛdeɛ ɛbɛma ideas no yɛ brief, nanso ɛmmfaso, efisɛ modern English pɛ concise. Exceptions: Verbs like 'suggest' ne 'recommend' nni hɔ a wɔde subjunctive; wɔ colloquial usage mu, indicative ɛyɛ (e.g., 'suggests that the data are...'). Fa 'in order to' (de 'to') ne 'due to the fact that' (de 'because') a ɛyɛ den.

translations.tw: Asɛm a ɛtɔ Nwoma ne Nnɔmba

title: Idiomatic Expressions & Colloquialisms / Mmebusɛm ne Abasɛm
bridge: Wɔ Twi, yɛbɛyɛ mmerɛw a wɔde kyerɛwfoɔ kyerɛ atɛnkyea (sɛ 'wɔ a wɔ nnie' vs. 'to be in the clouds'), nanso ɛbɛyɛ pɛ sɛ wɔatwe mmebusɛm pii ntɛm. Twi kasafoɔ bɛka sɛ wɔde 'tener' + noun (tener hambre) kɔ so maa wɔkasa, na ɛma wɔbɔ mmara sɛ 'I have hunger' na ɛnnye 'I'm hungry'. Ansa na, English abasɛm de phrasal verbs ne mmebusɛm a ɛnni sɛnkyerɛnne wɔ Twi, enti ɛsɛ sɛ wɔnntumu wɔn sɛdeɛ wɔwɔ kwan so, na ɛnyɛ sɛdeɛ wɔde twi ma wɔaka. Fa akoma yie mmebusɛm a wɔde ama ne pragmatics: mmebusɛm bi wɔ hɔ a wɔwɔ abasɛm pii ne a wɔte nkyerɛkyerɛ so.
rule: Saa ɛbɛyɛ C1, ɛsɛ sɛ wɔmfa mmebusɛm ne abasɛm a wɔwɔ kwan so wɔ kasa biara. Mmebusɛm ne mmerɛw a wɔn kyerɛwfoɔ nni sɛdeɛ wɔde wɔn akyi kyerɛ (sɛ 'break the ice' = 'romper el hielo'). Wɔ English, mmerɛw pii de verb ne preposition ma wɔaka, na ɛnyɛ sɛdeɛ wɔde Twi ma wɔaka. Sua mmebusɛm no nyinaa, na ɛnyɛ sɛdeɛ wɔde twi ma wɔaka, na fa akoma yie kyerɛwfoɔ: mmebusɛm bi wɔ hɔ a wɔwɔ abasɛm (sɛ 'gonna', 'wanna') na wɔn a wɔwɔ nnwuma (sɛ 'to commence'). Mmebusɛm biara wɔ hɔ a wɔwɔ akwantu: nsɛm pɔteɛ ne irony ne understatement wɔ British ne American English. Ma wɔabɔ mmara, sua kyerɛwfoɔ a wɔwɔ kwan so ne ma wɔakompa wɔn ne Twi mmebusɛm a wɔde kyerɛ.

concept_examples.text: It's not my cup of tea, but thanks for the offer.
concept_examples.translation: Ɛnyɛ me ho a, nanso meda wo akɔnta.
concept_examples.phonetic: ɪts nɒt maɪ kʌp əv tiː, bʌt θæŋks fər ði ˈɒfər.

concept_examples.text: Let's call it a day; we've been working for hours.
concept_examples.translation: Ma yɛnka da no ayɛ; yɛayɛ wɔ a wɔ no mu berɛ a wɔ no mu.
concept_examples.phonetic: lɛts kɔːl ɪt ə deɪ; wiːv bɪn ˈwɜːkɪŋ fər aʊəz.

concept_examples.text: She's over the moon about her promotion.
concept_examples.translation: Ɛyɛ paa no ara sɛ wɔde no ma no.
concept_examples.phonetic: ʃiːz ˈəʊvə ðə muːn əˈbaʊt hɜː prəˈməʊʃən.

concept_examples.text: I'm feeling under the weather today, so I'll stay home.
concept_examples.translation: Me nni me ho paa, enti mɛgye me ho wɔ hɔ.
concept_examples.phonetic: aɪm ˈfiːlɪŋ ˈʌndə ðə ˈwɛðər təˈdeɪ, səʊ aɪl steɪ həʊm.

common_error.wrong: I'm in the clouds thinking about my vacation.
common_error.correct: I'm on cloud nine thinking about my vacation.
common_error.correct_alt: I'm over the moon about my vacation.
common_error.explanation: Mmara no yɛ sɛ wɔde Twi 'wɔ a wɔ nnie' (wɔ a wɔ nnie) ma wɔaka English. Wɔ English, 'to be in the clouds' ɛnyɛ mmebusɛm a wɔde; wɔde 'to be on cloud nine' ma wɔaka anigye paa, na 'to have your head in the clouds' ma wɔaka sɛ wɔ a wɔ nnie. Ma wɔakɔso mmara no, sua mmebusɛm no nyinaa ne ma wɔato wɔn kyerɛwfoɔ wɔ akwan biara so ne ma wɔato wɔn kyerɛwfoɔ wɔ Twi mmebusɛm a wɔde kyerɛ.

levels.label: Common Idioms
levels.translation: Mmebusɛm a wɔwɔ kwan so

examples.original: It's a piece of cake, don't worry.
examples.phonetic: ɪts ə piːs əv keɪk, dəʊnt ˈwʌri.
examples.translation: Ɛyɛ adwuma a ɛyɛ den, ɛnyɛ sɛ wɔbɛyɛ.
examples.note: Wɔde ma wɔakyerɛ sɛ adwuma no yɛ den. Fa akoma yie sɛ wɔ Twi wɔka 'adwuma a ɛyɛ den', nanso wɔ English wɔka 'a piece of cake'.

examples.original: He finally spilled the beans about the surprise.
examples.phonetic: hiː ˈfaɪnəli spɪld ðə biːnz əˈbaʊt ðə səˈpraɪz.
examples.translation: Ɛda a wɔde no ma wɔakyerɛ sɛ wɔde no ma wɔakyerɛ.
examples.note: 'Spill the beans' kyerɛ sɛ wɔde no ma wɔakyerɛ. Ɛnyɛ sɛ 'derramar los frijoles' sɛdeɛ wɔde Twi ma wɔaka.

examples.original: Just hit the sack; you look exhausted.
examples.phonetic: dʒʌst hɪt ðə sæk; juː lʊk ɪɡˈzɔːstɪd.
examples.translation: Fa wo ho kɔe; ɛyɛ paa sɛ wɔde no ma wɔakyerɛ.
examples.note: Abasɛm. 'Hit the sack' = fa wo ho kɔe. Ɛte sɛ 'irse al sobre' wɔ Spain (abasɛm).

levels.label: Colloquial Phrasal Verbs
levels.translation: Phrasal verbs a wɔwɔ abasɛm

examples.original: We need to figure out a solution to this problem.
examples.phonetic: wiː niːd tə ˈfɪɡər aʊt ə səˈluːʃən tə ðɪs ˈprɒbləm.
examples.translation: Yɛsɛ sɛ yɛhu adwuma a ɛyɛ den.
examples.note: 'Figure out' = hu, sua. Ɛte sɛ 'dar con' wɔ Twi. Ɛyɛ separable: sua 'figure it out'.

examples.original: I can't put up with this noise anymore.
examples.phonetic: aɪ kɑːnt pʊt ʌp wɪð ðɪs nɔɪz ˌɛnɪˈmɔː.
examples.translation: Mennka sɛ mɛkɔ so ma wɔde no ma wɔakyerɛ.
examples.note: 'Put up with' = kɔ so, sua. Wɔ Twi wɔka 'aguantar' anaa 'soportar'. Ɛnyɛ sɛ 'put up' (kɔ so).

examples.original: Let's meet up later and catch up on everything.
examples.phonetic: lɛts miːt ʌp ˈleɪtər ənd kætʃ ʌp ɒn ˈɛvrɪθɪŋ.
examples.translation: Ma yɛnka da no ayɛ ne ma yɛnka da no ayɛ.
examples.note: 'Meet up' = kɔ da, 'catch up' = ma yɛnka da no ayɛ. Wɔ Twi wɔde verb bi ma wɔaka, nanso wɔ English wɔde phrasal verbs ma wɔaka wɔ kasa mu.

levels.label: Idioms for Everyday Situations
levels.translation: Mmebusɛm a wɔwɔ adwuma biara mu

examples.original: You're pulling my leg, that can't be true!
examples.phonetic: jʊər ˈpʊlɪŋ maɪ lɛɡ, ðæt kɑːnt biː truː.
examples.translation: Wɔde me ma wɔakyerɛ, ɛnyɛ sɛ wɔde no ma wɔakyerɛ!
examples.note: Ɛte sɛ 'tomar el pelo'. Wɔde ma wɔakyerɛ sɛ wɔde no ma wɔakyerɛ. Fa akoma yie: ɛnyɛ 'pull my leg' sɛdeɛ wɔde Twi ma wɔaka.

examples.original: Let's get this show on the road – we have a tight schedule.
examples.phonetic: lɛts ɡɛt ðɪs ʃəʊ ɒn ðə rəʊd – wiː hæv ə taɪt ˈʃɛdjuːl.
examples.translation: Ma yɛnka da no ayɛ – yɛayɛ wɔ a wɔ no mu berɛ a wɔ no mu.
examples.note: 'Get the show on the road' = kɔ da. Wɔ Twi: 'ponerse en marcha' anaa 'arrancar'.

examples.original: The exam was a whole different ball game.
examples.phonetic: ði ɪɡˈzæm wɒz ə həʊl ˈdɪfrənt bɔːl ɡeɪm.
examples.translation: Adwuma no yɛ den paa.
examples.note: 'A different ball game' = adwuma bi a ɛyɛ den paa. Wɔde ma wɔakompa adwuma biara.

translations.tw: Abasɛm ne mmebusɛm a wɔwɔ kwan so

title: Hedging and Softening Strategies for Near-Native Fluency / Nkyerɛase ne Nnɔmba Kyɛfa a Wɔde Kyerɛw Nnɔpa-Anigye Kasa
bridge: Wɔ Twi, yɛde nkyerɛase bɛbɛ kɛse kɛse wɔ ‘sɛ’, ‘sɛ obi’, ne subjunctive tense ma yɛn kasa tɔ so da. Wɔ English, wɔde modal verbs (might, could), adverbs wɔ ‘perhaps’ ne ‘probably’, ne introductory phrases wɔ ‘I was wondering’ anaa ‘It seems like’ ma wɔn kasa tɔ so da. Ɛbɛn na ɔkɔ so pi ara ne sɛ, wɔbɛka subjunctive tense a ɛwɔ Twi nea ɛnte sa wɔ English, anaa wɔde tone bi a ɛte sɛn ara wɔ kasa. Sɛ woka sɛe yi a, ɛbɛma woka te sɛ obi a ɔte pa ne a ɔte sɛn wɔ formal ne informal contexts.
rule: Wɔ English, wɔde nnɔmba kyɛfa (hedging) ma wɔn kasa tɔ so da: 1) Modal verbs: 'might', 'could', 'would' (e.g. 'That might be an issue' vs. 'That is an issue'). 2) Adverbs ne phrases: 'perhaps', 'maybe', 'probably', 'apparently', 'as far as I know'. 3) Introductory phrases a wɔde ma wɔn kasa tɔ so da: 'I was wondering if...', 'I'm not sure, but...', 'It seems to me that...'. 4) Opinion verbs a wɔn ho nhia da: 'I'd say', 'I tend to think'. 5) Tag questions ma obi kyerɛw so: '..., isn't it?' (nanso wɔ C1, wɔpɛ tone a ɛte sɛn pi). Ɛfiri Twi, wɔmmusubjective tense ma wɔn kasa tɔ so da; wɔde sentence structure ne word choice ma wɔn kasa tɔ so da. Wɔ formal contexts, wɔde complex constructions wɔ ‘I'd venture to say’ anaa ‘It could be argued that’. Wɔ informal contexts, wɔde filler words wɔ ‘sort of’, ‘kind of’, ‘you know’.

concept_examples.text: I was wondering if you might consider a later start time.
concept_examples.translation: Mepɛ sɛ mebisa wo sɛ wubetumi adi kan a ɛbɛyɛ paa.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪ wəz ˈwʌndərɪŋ ɪf ju ˈmaɪt kənˈsɪdər ə ˈleɪtər stɑːrt taɪm/

concept_examples.text: It seems like there could be a problem with the schedule.
concept_examples.translation: Ɛte sɛ ɛyɛ sɛ ɛyɛ problem bi wɔ timetable no ho.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɪt siːmz laɪk ðər kʊd bi ə ˈprɑːbləm wɪð ðə ˈskedʒuːl/

concept_examples.text: That might not be the best approach, if you ask me.
concept_examples.translation: Sɛ wubisa me a, ɛte sɛ ɛyɛ sɛ ɛnte paa approach no ho.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ðæt maɪt nɑːt bi ðə best əˈproʊtʃ, ɪf ju æsk miː/

common_error.wrong: I think that is a mistake.
common_error.correct: I'd say that might be a mistake.
common_error.correct_alt: It could be a mistake, possibly.
common_error.explanation: Wɔ Twi, ‘Mepɛ sɛ ɛyɛ mistake’ ɛte sɛn ara ne ɛyɛ paa, nanso wɔ English, ɛte sɛ ɛyɛ kɛse wɔ diplomatic contexts. Native speakers de modal (might, could) ne adverb (possibly, maybe) ma wɔn kasa tɔ so da. Mma wɔ ‘I think’ no ho kɔ so pi, na wɔde structures wɔ ‘I'd say’, ‘It seems to me’, anaa ‘I'm inclined to think’ ma wɔn kasa vari.

levels.label: Modal Verbs for Softening
levels.translation: Modal Verbs ma Kasa Tɔ So Da

examples.original: He might have forgotten the meeting.
examples.phonetic: /hiː maɪt həv fərˈɡɑːtən ðə ˈmiːtɪŋ/
examples.translation: Ɛte sɛ ɔrebu meeting no.
examples.note: Modal 'might' kyerɛkyerɛ uncertainty a ɛte sɛn ara, sɛ ‘sɛ’ a ɛwɔ Twi, nanso ɛnte subjunctive.

examples.original: You could try calling her again.
examples.phonetic: /juː kʊd traɪ ˈkɔːlɪŋ hɜːr əˈɡen/
examples.translation: Wubetumi adi awerɛw wo nea ɔbɛyɛ paa.
examples.note: 'Could' de ma suggestion a ɛte sɛn ara, ɛte paa wɔ ‘you should’.

examples.original: I would say that's a fair point.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ wʊd seɪ ðæts ə fer pɔɪnt/
examples.translation: Mede kyerɛ sɛ ɛyɛ point a ɛte paa.
examples.note: 'I would say' ma opinion no tɔ so da ne ɛma ɛnte absolute sɛ ‘I say’.

levels.label: Adverbs and Hedging Phrases
levels.translation: Adverbs ne Phrases a Wɔde Ma Kasa Tɔ So Da

examples.original: Perhaps we should reconsider the plan.
examples.phonetic: /pərˈhæps wiː ʃʊd ˌriːkənˈsɪdər ðə plæn/
examples.translation: Ɛte sɛ yɛbɛyɛ reconsideration wɔ plan no ho.
examples.note: 'Perhaps' ɛte paa wɔ ‘maybe’ ne wɔde ma ɛkɔ so wɔ sentence no anim anaa ntɛm.

examples.original: It's probably going to rain later.
examples.phonetic: /ɪts ˈprɑːbəbli ˈɡoʊɪŋ tə reɪn ˈleɪtər/
examples.translation: Ɛte sɛ ɛbɛsoa ntɛm baabi.
examples.note: Wɔ Twi, ‘probably’ de ma subjunctive, nanso wɔ English, wɔde adverb no ma.

examples.original: As far as I know, the project is on track.
examples.phonetic: /æz fɑːr æz aɪ noʊ, ðə ˈprɑːdʒekt ɪz ɑːn træk/
examples.translation: Sɛ mebisa a, project no rekyekye sɛ wɔaka no.
examples.note: Phrase yi ma information no tɔ so da ne ɛma ɛte sɛn ara wɔ diplomacy.

levels.label: Indirect Questions and Diplomacy
levels.translation: Indirect Questions ne Diplomacy

examples.original: I was wondering if you'd be free for a chat tomorrow.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ wəz ˈwʌndərɪŋ ɪf juːd biː friː fər ə tʃæt təˈmɑːroʊ/
examples.translation: Mepɛ sɛ mebisa wo sɛ wubetumi adi kan wɔ chat bi ara ntɛm.
examples.note: Past tense 'I was' ma question no tɔ so da ne ɛma ɛte sɛn ara wɔ ‘I am’.

examples.original: Would it be possible to move the deadline?
examples.phonetic: /wʊd ɪt bi ˈpɑːsəbl tə muːv ðə ˈdedlaɪn/
examples.translation: Ɛyɛ sɛ ɛyɛ sɛ wubetumi adi deadline no?
examples.note: Conditional 'would' ma request no tɔ so da ne ɛma ɛnte direct sɛ ‘Can you move...’.

examples.original: I'm not entirely sure, but I think the data might be outdated.
examples.phonetic: /aɪm nɑːt ɪnˈtaɪərli ʃʊr, bʌt aɪ θɪŋk ðə ˈdeɪtə maɪt bi ˌaʊtˈdeɪtɪd/
examples.translation: Mennim paa, nanso mede kyerɛ sɛ data no betumi ayɛ old.
examples.note: Sɛ wɔka expression a ɛte sɛn ara wɔ doubt ne modal a, ɛma ɛte sɛn ara wɔ hedging.

translations.tw: Nkyerɛase ne Nnɔmba Kyɛfa a Wɔde Kyerɛw Nnɔpa-Anigye Kasa
